I am a 60-year-old farmer in North West Nigeria, and I have been farming this land for many years. My beans plot is intercropped with millet as I always do, because the millet gives me food for the household while the beans put nitrogen back into my sandy soil. I will apply a small amount of NPK fertilizer that I managed to get through the subsidy program, and I will also spread cow manure that I collected during the dry season to help the soil. For seed, I am using my own saved seed from last year because the improved varieties from the agro-dealers are too expensive and hard to find. I will spray some pesticide because the bean pod borer and aphids always attack my cowpea; without it I lose too much. I will not irrigate because I have no pump and this plot is not near the fadama. My wives and children will do most of the work, but I may hire a few young men to help with weeding when the rains come.
